## What The Business Is

Strategy Inc. (formerly MicroStrategy) is now primarily a **Bitcoin treasury company** with a legacy enterprise analytics/software business. Management describes the core model as raising capital through common equity, preferred equity/“digital credit,” and other instruments to accumulate and hold bitcoin over the long term. In its Q1 2026 materials, Strategy said it held **818,334 BTC** as of early May 2026, representing about **3.9% of the maximum bitcoin supply**, and characterized itself as the largest corporate bitcoin holder. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000024/mstr-20260505x8kxex991.htm?utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

Operationally, Strategy still sells analytics and application software, but the market’s focus is overwhelmingly on its bitcoin balance sheet and capital-markets engine. The Q1 2026 call excerpt emphasizes management’s objective to grow **bitcoin per share** via repeated BTC purchases funded by securities issuance, while keeping leverage “modest” relative to the bitcoin reserve. The company has also built a stack of preferred securities—STRF, STRC, STRK, STRD—positioned by management as “Digital Credit” products backed by Strategy’s bitcoin-heavy capital structure. ([assets.contentstack.io](https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltf8d808d9b8cebd37/bltb120ca8ac738e134/69fa4a3250829712e58cb255/strategy-q1-2026-financial-results.pdf?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Strategy continued adding bitcoin after Q1. On June 8, 2026, it disclosed **845,256 BTC** held after buying **1,550 BTC** during June 1–7, funded by ATM proceeds, with aggregate BTC cost of about **$64.0B** and average cost around **$75,680/BTC**. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526260709/mstr-20260504.htm?utm_source=openai))

The company kept expanding its capital toolkit. On June 29, 2026, Strategy announced a **Digital Credit Capital Framework**, a USD reserve policy, a higher STRC dividend policy, up to **$1.0B** of repurchase authorization for digital-credit securities, up to **$1.0B** for MSTR common repurchases, and a BTC monetization program. Management framed the framework as designed to strengthen preferred securities, enhance liquidity, and preserve long-term bitcoin exposure. ([markets.financialcontent.com](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/bizwire-2026-6-29-strategy-announces-digital-credit-capital-framework-usd-reserve-policy-strc-dividend-policy-digital-credit-and-mstr-repurchase-authorizations-and-btc-monetization-program?utm_source=openai))

Strategy also rebuilt liquidity late in June: disclosures around June 22 reported **847,363 BTC** and a **$1.4B USD Reserve**, and coverage noted the reserve later increased to roughly **$2.55B** as part of the new framework. ([strategy.com](https://www.strategy.com/press/strategy-increases-its-usd-reserve-to-1-4-billion-and-btc-reserve-to-847363_06-22-2026?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Q1 2026 results showed the downside of fair-value bitcoin accounting: Strategy reported a large operating and net loss in the transcript excerpt, driven mainly by a decline in bitcoin’s quarter-end fair value. The company’s Q1 release said digital assets had a market value of about **$64.1B** as of May 1, but quarter-end results reflected earlier bitcoin weakness. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000024/mstr-20260505x8kxex991.htm?utm_source=openai))

The capital structure is increasingly complex and cash-demanding. Preferred securities carry high dividend obligations; recent disclosures raised STRC’s annualized dividend rate to **12.00%** for semi-monthly periods beginning July 2026, and management now explicitly evaluates BTC monetization as one tool to support obligations and capital allocation. ([markets.financialcontent.com](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/bizwire-2026-6-29-strategy-announces-digital-credit-capital-framework-usd-reserve-policy-strc-dividend-policy-digital-credit-and-mstr-repurchase-authorizations-and-btc-monetization-program?utm_source=openai))

A notable shift occurred in early July: Strategy disclosed bitcoin sales to fund preferred dividends, with reports citing **3,588 BTC sold for about $216M**. That contrasts with the company’s historical “buy and hold” narrative and may increase scrutiny of whether future preferred obligations require more BTC monetization during weak market conditions. ([bitcoinmagazine.com](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/strategy-mstr-sells-3588-bitcoin?utm_source=openai))

The common stock was also volatile: one recent market report said MSTR fell **45.4% in June 2026**, reflecting sensitivity to bitcoin prices, preferred-dividend concerns, and changing perceptions of the treasury model. ([fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/05/why-strategy-inc-plunged-in-june/?utm_source=openai))

## Transcript Read — Long Case

- Stretch (STRC) has $8.5B outstanding, is the largest tradable preferred, trading with 3 vol and 11.5% yield; demand accelerating (e.g., $2.2B raised in one week in April).
- BTC yield YTD of 9.4% with acceleration (6% in April), on track to exceed 10% annual target and double BTC per share in 7 years.
- Clear plan to retire all convertible debt, potentially boosting BTC per share and reducing credit risk.
- Management explicitly stated willingness to sell BTC to capture $2.2B tax asset and fund dividends, which could be more accretive than equity sales at low mNAV.
- Stretch is being integrated into major credit ETFs (e.g., BlackRock's PFF as #2 holding), tokenized products, and seeing rapid institutional and retail adoption.
- Risk model shows investment-grade credit profile even with conservative BTC assumptions, supporting Stretch scalability.

Rationale: Stretch (STRC) success is a major positive, raising $8.5B in 9 months with low vol and high Sharpe ratio, providing a durable, low-dilution funding source. BTC yield accelerated to 9.4% YTD (6% in April alone), on pace to exceed 10% annual target. Management outlined clear optionalities, including selling BTC to unlock $2.2B tax asset, retiring converts, and enhancing BTC per share accretion. The digital credit ecosystem is expanding rapidly, with Stretch being integrated into ETFs and tokenized products.

- STRC ("Stretch") has become a genuine capital-markets franchise: $8.5B raised in 9 months, ETF inclusion (top holding in PFF), and accelerating institutional demand gives Strategy a durable, low-dilution funding channel.
- BTC yield of 9.4% YTD (6% in April alone) is tracking above the 10% annual target — bitcoin-per-share compounding is intact, and the plan to retire converts reduces credit risk.
- The June Digital Credit Capital Framework ($2.55B USD reserve, $1B preferred buyback, $1B MSTR buyback authorization) gives management tools to defend mNAV and the preferred complex; buying back stock below NAV is accretive.
- Any bitcoin recovery flows through with leverage: at 847k BTC, each $10k/BTC move is ~$8.5B of NAV, dwarfing the operating business.

## Bear Case
- The "never sell" narrative is broken: 3,588 BTC sold in July (~$216M) to fund preferred dividends. STRC's dividend was hiked to 12% — a rising, mandatory cash drain (~$1B+/yr on STRC alone) against a business with negative operating FCF (-$88M TTM).
- Q1 net loss of $12.8B underscores extreme BTC sensitivity; the stock fell 45% in June. mNAV at ~1.27x (and compressing) makes equity issuance close to dilutive, weakening the flywheel that drove the premium.
- If BTC stays weak, the model inverts: forced BTC monetization to service preferreds, shrinking BTC/share, further mNAV compression — a reflexive downward spiral.
- The software business (~$490M revenue, flat for 3 years) cannot support the capital structure and provides no valuation floor.

- **12-month forward multiple:** **-600x** (mechanical output of my EV target of ~$36B on forecast forward FCF of -$60M).
- **Direction: CONTRACT** — I am contracting the effective valuation (EV falls ~10% despite a modest FCF improvement).
- **Drivers:** (1) mNAV premium compression from ~1.27x toward ~1.05x as BTC sales to fund 12% preferred dividends break the HODL narrative and impair the accretive-issuance flywheel; (2) rising fixed obligations (preferred dividends) against negative operating FCF force ongoing monetization in weak tape; (3) the STRC franchise and buyback authorizations are partial offsets, preventing a full de-rating to 1.0x NAV, but the June framework is already largely priced.

- **mNAV compression:** At ~1.27x mNAV post-Q1 (and lower after June's drawdown), equity issuance approaches dilutive territory (~1.22x breakeven), throttling the primary accretion engine. Q1's $12.8B net loss shows the fair-value accounting whipsaw.

- **Balance-sheet optionality**: 847k+ BTC (~3.9% of max supply), a $2.55B USD reserve, $2.2B tax asset that BTC sales can unlock, $1B common + $1B digital-credit buyback authorizations, and a path to retire converts — all accretive to BTC per share if executed at low mNAV.

## Bear Case

## Bull Case

Strategy's value is not its software FCF but its bitcoin treasury (~845K+ BTC) and its capital-markets engine. The bull thesis rests on continued mNAV premium (>1.2x), accelerating BTC-per-share yield (9.4% YTD, targeting >10%), and the Stretch/STRC "Digital Credit" franchise raising low-cost, low-dilution capital ($8.5B in 9 months, ETF integration). If BTC rallies over the next 12 months, the equity re-rates sharply given its embedded leverage, and the premium-to-NAV expands. Convertible debt retirement reduces credit risk and boosts BTC/share.

## Bear Case

The July 2026 BTC sales (3,588 BTC) to fund preferred dividends break the "HODL" narrative and expose the core fragility: 12% STRC dividends and fixed obligations demand perpetual capital raising or BTC appreciation. With mNAV compressed to ~1.27x (breakeven ~1.22x), equity issuance is barely accretive and can turn dilutive. MSTR fell 45% in June 2026. TTM net loss of $12.2B from BTC fair-value marks illustrates extreme downside convexity. If BTC weakens, dividend coverage, credit spreads, and the premium all deteriorate simultaneously — a reflexive downward spiral.

## Multiple Re-Rating

FCF is negative (TTM FCF = -$88.29M), so EV/FCF is not a meaningful valuation anchor for this asset — the business is a levered BTC proxy, not an FCF compounder. The "current implied multiple" is EV/TTM FCF = 40,167.7 / -88.29 = **-455.0x** (meaningless/negative). Applying a negative FCF multiple produces nonsense, so I anchor forward market cap on the mNAV/BTC-treasury framework and then bridge, but report the mechanical multiple for format compliance.

- **Current implied multiple:** -455.0x (EV/TTM FCF, negative — non-informative)
- **12-month forward multiple:** -430.0x (applied to still-negative forward FCF)
- **Direction:** contract (toward zero, i.e., less negative) — reflecting slightly less FCF drag but no path to positive FCF
- **Top drivers:** (1) The multiple is meaningless with negative FCF; real driver is mNAV compression from ~1.27x toward ~1.15x as the BTC-sale narrative erodes premium; (2) rising 12% preferred dividend cash burn and BTC monetization pressure; (3) post-45% June drawdown, index/flow deleveraging and reflexive risk regime.

## Logic

With negative FCF, I value MSTR as a BTC-treasury vehicle. Forward FCF stays modestly negative (~-$95M) as dividend/opex drag persists despite software stability. I take a mNAV-based view: current market cap $34,119.6M sits on ~845K BTC. Over 12 months I assume roughly flat-to-modestly-higher BTC value but a compressing premium (mNAV 1.27x → ~1.12x) due to the broken HODL narrative, dividend-funding sales, and elevated volatility. Net effect: market cap roughly flat to slightly down from current, landing near **$33,000M**.

Applying the mechanical (negative) forward multiple of -430x to forward FCF of -$90.8M gives EV ≈ $39,044M — reconciled. Forward market cap = 39,044 − 6,048 ≈ **$32,996M**.

Strategy’s bull case is that the market continues to value it less as a software company and more as a scaled Bitcoin treasury/capital-markets platform. The company has a very large BTC position, continued BTC accumulation, and a developing “Digital Credit” preferred stack that could provide recurring, lower-common-dilution funding if investor demand remains strong. If STRC/other preferred securities keep gaining ETF/index adoption and the company can retire converts while maintaining BTC-per-share growth above its stated target, the equity could regain some mNAV premium despite weak reported earnings and negative FCF.

The disclosed BTC sales to fund preferred dividends weaken the “permanent HODL” narrative, and high preferred dividend obligations create a recurring cash burden that may require either continued capital markets access or additional BTC monetization. With mNAV already relatively compressed and the common highly sensitive to BTC price, sustained BTC weakness could pressure credit spreads, funding capacity, and equity issuance economics. 2. **Capital-structure complexity and high cost of capital:** 11–12% preferred yields and dividend obligations should keep the equity risk premium elevated.
3. **Digital-credit adoption is real but partly priced:** STRC growth and ETF inclusion support the model, but they are not enough to justify holding the current extreme negative-FCF multiple.

I forecast 12-month forward FCF of **-$120.0M**, modestly worse than the current TTM **-$88.29M**. STRC / “Digital Credit” adoption, ETF inclusion, and management’s ability to raise preferred or equity capital could support continued BTC-per-share growth without relying solely on common dilution. If bitcoin strengthens and credit spreads remain receptive, the stock can regain a higher mNAV premium despite weak accounting earnings and negative FCF.

## Bear Case

The bear case is that the model’s durability is increasingly questioned. The disclosed BTC sales to fund preferred dividends weaken the “permanent HODL” narrative, while high preferred dividend obligations make the capital structure more cash-demanding. With mNAV around 1.27x in the packet, the accretive issuance window is narrower, and a bitcoin drawdown could simultaneously pressure asset value, credit appetite, and the company’s ability to fund dividends without more BTC monetization. Legacy software FCF is too small to anchor valuation.

1. **Narrative compression:** BTC sales to fund dividends make the treasury model look less pristine and reduce willingness to pay an extreme optical multiple.
2. **Growth durability slowing:** BTC-per-share growth remains possible, but at 845k+ BTC and lower mNAV, incremental accretion becomes harder and more dependent on receptive capital markets.
3. **Capital structure / rates pressure:** high preferred yields and complex digital-credit obligations should cap the multiple, even if STRC adoption remains a real offset.

TTM FCF is negative `-$88.29m`.
